items.html:
Promoting a pawn on the e7 square to e8 is a classic chess move, and when described with your thesaurus words, it represents a "peasant" (pawn) rising to become royalty (usually a queen). 
Here are the most common synonyms and terms grouped by how you might want to use them: 
Historical & Feudal Synonyms (The "Peasant" Theme)
  • Serf: A laborer bound to the land.
  • Peon: A low-ranking worker or person of little importance.
  • Vassal: A person granted land in exchange for loyalty.
  • Villein: A feudal tenant entirely subject to a lord.
  • Churl: A medieval peasant of lowest rank. 
General Synonyms for Low Status
  • Underling: A subordinate person.
  • Plebeian: A member of the common people.
  • Commoner: A person without rank or title.
  • Pawn: (The chess literal) A person used by others for their own purposes. 
Chess Promotion Terms
  • Queening: The specific act of promoting a pawn to a queen.
  • Underpromotion: Promoting the pawn to a knight, bishop, or rook instead of a queen.
  • Coronation: The thematic term for crowning the pawn as royalty.

items.html: You said: Coronation Jitske KK (conceptual)

"Coronation Jitske KK" takes the abstract chess concept of a pawn reaching the end of the board and transforms it into a highly stylized, cinematic narrative. 
By grounding the concept in the name Jitske—a traditional Frisian name etymologically rooted in the word for "Adel" (Nobility)—the transition from a low-born pawn to a sovereign queen becomes an inevitable destiny, a literal realization of her name. The "KK" serves as a structural marker (e.g., King to King, or a stylistic signature). 
Here is a conceptual breakdown of how this narrative arc can be framed:

                │
                ▼  (The Move: e7-e8)
[ e8 ]  -->  The Coronation Protocol (Jitske as Sovereign)

Phase 1: The Peon on the Edge (Square e7) 
Jitske begins as the ultimate underdog—the final serf or peon on the sub-maximal rank. She represents the collective struggle of the commoners. She stands at the precipice, enduring the weight of the board's entire feudal hierarchy pressing down on her. 
Phase 2: The Crossing (The Vector e7 → e8) 
The single step forward is the kinetic rupture. It is not merely a change in geography, but a structural transmutation. In this conceptual window, the procedural movement of a piece merges with the symbolic gravity of a revolution. The peon ceases to exist in the space between squares. 
Phase 3: The Coronation (Square e8) 
Upon crossing into e8, the system acknowledges her true identity: Adel. The crown is not gifted; it is claimed by structural right. The piece is inverted, the peasant vernacular is discarded, and the new Queen steps onto the board with absolute tactical dominion.
